problem: Open-vocabulary ObjectNav executors (VLFM, ApexNav) search for one active target. Multi-object work (MultiON, SAM, OneMap) focuses on visiting order and memory. Neither decides how to split a shared, finite action budget among several unresolved semantic requests, so one low-yield or infeasible request can monopolize the horizon and leave present targets unreachable.
motivation: In a multi-goal mission every action spent on one request shortens the others' horizon. An untouched goal can therefore become effectively undiscoverable purely because budget was consumed elsewhere, a state dimension that single-goal search lacks. Heuristic arbitration (fixed scores, bandits, RL) does not estimate calibrated, budget-conditioned completion probabilities. Such probabilities are needed to decide both which goal gets effort next and when to permanently drop a goal.
key_idea: Estimate for each unresolved goal a calibrated, budget-conditioned completion curve F_g(b|h_t) from navigation telemetry. Its value at the remaining budget (remaining discoverability) drives conservative irreversible ABORT, and its marginal slope (expected completions per action) drives reversible PERSIST/SWITCH. COMMIT is handled by a separate SPRT-style local verifier, all above a frozen executor.
insight: Separating reversible allocation (point-estimate marginal return) from irreversible decisions (conservative threshold on calibrated belief, plus a sequential likelihood-ratio verifier) works because allocation mistakes can be undone while aborts cannot. The component that matters most is budget conditioning. Replacing it with fixed-horizon discoverability drops HM3D/ApexNav CR from .414 to .395 and raises WSF from .548 to .585, the largest ablation drop. Removing the semantic feature gives .401, and a uniform π0=.5 gives .409 (CR stays in [.404,.414] across π0 ∈ {.3,.5,.7,.9}). The executor's semantic score helps only as one feature among geometry, coverage and search history (hazard AUC .692 → .748). The belief is calibrated (Brier .132, ECE .034 on intervention-independent Sequential replays) and transfers without refitting. The advantage over a fixed-score arbiter grows with the number of competing goals (+3.4 → +5.8 CR from K=2 to K=5) and under infeasible requests, which is where calibrated belief and fixed thresholds disagree most.
method: Remaining discoverability: b_g(t)=F_g(B_rem|h_t), the probability that the frozen executor completes goal g if b more (non-contiguous) primitive actions are allocated to it. It is monotone in budget, so it decays when other goals consume actions.

Calibrated local completion hazard: d_g(v)=σ(θᵀx_g(v)), a logistic regression over [newly observable area, map distance to frontier/proposal, camera-bearing cosine, rank-normalized executor semantic score, goal-frontier coverage, normalized effort spent, bias]. The positive label is completion within N_d=15 actions after visiting v, fit on 16 HM3D dev scenes. No GT target geometry is used.

Bayesian discoverability update: a Beta(1,1)-smoothed per-category prior π0^g is updated by unsuccessful inspections as π_t ∝ π0 ∏(1−d_g(v_i)). Views are NMS-separated by ≥0.5 m / 30° to approximate independence, and the posterior persists through suspension.

Completion-curve construction: candidate viewpoints are sorted by d_g(v)/c_search(v), where c_search is primitive-action path cost including turns. F_g(u)=π_t[1−∏_{prefix within budget u}(1−d_g(v))], piecewise-linearly interpolated, which yields a non-decreasing concave curve.

Marginal-return arbitration (PERSIST/SWITCH): greedy online analogue of the KKT equal-marginal-return condition for separable concave allocation. The index I_{g→h}=max_v π_t^h d_h(v)/(c_search(v)+c_switch(g,h)) uses a switch cost equal to the dev-log excess relocation overhead. It is re-evaluated every 20 actions, with a 20-action grace period for hysteresis.
Conservative ABORT: permanently remove the active goal only if F_g(B_rem)<ε_min=0.05 AND some other goal has a higher index. This keeps the best goal when all are hard.

SPRT-inspired COMMIT verifier: accumulate clipped (ℓ_max=2) log-likelihood ratios of encounter evidence from dev-fit densities p1/p0 at separated viewpoints. Commit when Λ_g>log((1−β)/α) with α=.05, β=.10. Decision order per step is COMMIT → ABORT → SWITCH → PERSIST.

setting.training_data: Offline development logs of the frozen executor on 16 HM3D dev scenes (hazard labels, category completion priors, evidence densities, switch cost); no backbone or policy training; no refitting for MP3D, ApexNav transfer, or the real quadruped

numbers_note: No standard benchmark is used. All results are on the authors' own multi-goal mission sets built in Habitat on HM3D (16 dev / 64 held-out scenes, 5000 missions) and MP3D (2000 missions), plus 30 real-robot missions. The paper prints all metrics as fractions (e.g. .414); these are converted to 0-100 here. 'split' = test denotes held-out scenes, not an official split. Mechanism-validation numbers are given in text only and are not navigation results: hazard AUC .692 → .748; Brier/NLL/ECE .132/.386/.034 on HM3D/VLFM, .145/.414/.049 on MP3D/VLFM, .139/.401/.042 on HM3D/ApexNav; index sextile completion .047 → .321, AUC .705. Component ablations on HM3D/ApexNav are also text-only (CR/WSF): no semantic .401/.571, fixed-horizon .395/.585, uniform π0 .409/.557. Figures contain no extracted content.
results: BAT-Nav beats all baselines on every dataset/executor pair. The strongest baseline is ScoreArb, a fixed-score arbiter with the same telemetry and COMMIT verifier. On HM3D/ApexNav, CR goes from .372 to .414 and MGSR from .132 to .173. On HM3D/VLFM, CR goes from .345 to .384. The CR gains are +3.9/+4.2/+3.3/+3.9 points, all with bootstrap CIs excluding zero, and WSF, Steps/Comp and monopoly improve everywhere. PPO-Arbitrator reaches only .307 CR on HM3D/VLFM despite 2M online steps. The margin over ScoreArb grows from 3.4 to 5.8 CR points as K rises from 2 to 5. With 25% absent requests, abort precision/recall rise from .76/.68 to .89/.83 and median removal time falls from 102 to 68 actions. The same ordering holds on a real quadruped (CR .60 vs .57 vs .43 for Sequential).
limitations: Evaluated only on self-constructed multi-goal mission sets with self-implemented baselines (no GOAT-Bench/MultiON or published multi-goal methods). Absolute gains over the strongest baseline are modest (~3-6 CR points), and absolute CR stays low (≤.414) because the frozen executor bounds what reallocation can recover.

Requires offline development-log calibration of the hazard, evidence densities and switch cost for the executor. Large sensing shifts may need recalibration. The independence assumption behind the posterior update is only approximated via view suppression.
PPO baseline reported only with VLFM, and the real-robot study is small (30 missions, 3 layouts) with the executor unspecified.
